Additionally: node_modules was installable here, so a real tsc pass was run against a single-file tsconfig (strict, jsx react-jsx, @/* paths, plus --noUnusedLocals --noUnusedParameters). Result: only 3 errors, all TS2307 'Cannot find module' for @/components/Tag, @/lib/walletStore, @/components/EthIcon — files absent from this partial tree. Zero type errors in the code itself and zero unused locals, which also confirms no deleted constant is still referenced.

unverified: The app has NOT been run. No screen was rendered, no Tauri command was actually invoked, and no live Alchemy/Etherscan response was observed.

Types are only as verified as the note above: the 3 unstaged modules (Tag, EthIcon, loadWallets) resolve to `any`, so their call sites are not type-checked. Those call sites are unchanged from the original file except loadWallets(), which is still called as loadWallets()[0]?.address.
The shapes of PnlSummary / TradeRecord / NftPnlSummary / SisterReport were read from the Rust sources and from src/lib/tauri.ts; serde field naming was trusted, not observed on the wire.
Layout of the new bubble-map node placement (radial, up to 8 nodes in a 960x510 viewBox) was computed to stay in bounds arithmetically but never rendered.
Rate-limit behaviour is reasoned, not measured: the P&L tab issues 3 commands strictly sequentially and each tab fetches once, but no 429 test was possible.
notes: No new Rust was written and src-tauri/ was not touched. src/lib/tauri.ts was read only — every call goes through wrappers that already existed there (getPortfolioSnapshot, getPnlSummary, getTradeHistory, getNftPnl, findSisterWallets, getAssetTransfers, loadAlchemyKey); no direct invoke() was added.

Request budget: on mount exactly ONE command runs (get_portfolio_snapshot, for the always-visible header). Feed / P&L / Connections each fetch only when their tab is opened and only once per mount. The P&L tab awaits get_pnl_summary → get_trade_history → get_nft_pnl one at a time rather than Promise.all, because each of the first two performs transfer-heavy Alchemy calls. Nothing fans out per row.
get_nft_pnl is treated as an optional enrichment inside the P&L fetch: its failure sets a separate message under the breakdown table and does not blank the KPI row, chart or trade list.
Errors are never swallowed: every catch surfaces the Rust error string (errText keeps the original message) into the same red #ff8a96 treatment the collection screen uses.

Visual structure, grid templates, colours, spacing and section order are unchanged. Two label changes were necessary for truthfulness: Recent Trades column 'ETH' → 'Cost', and the connections legend 'Outflow/Inflow' → 'Sent to (tx)/Received from (tx)'. Two dead side-panel buttons ('Track Wallet', 'Create Alert') were replaced with working links ('Open in Monitor', 'View on Etherscan') because that panel was rebuilt entirely.
